aria: Animated recap of the Sixers' 127 to 121 road win at Chicago: LeBron James's record-setting 3-pointer in the first quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jaylen Brown's 29 points, the top scorers, how the Sixers won, and the next game against Boston.
notes: Box score from the Sixers' 127–121 win over the Chicago Bulls in Chicago on Nov 8, 2026, from StatMuse's full box score and the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via ABC News and CBS Chicago), Roundtable, NBC Sports Philadelphia, Philly Sports Reports, Liberty Ballers (via Yahoo Sports), Bleacher Report and Yardbarker. All 127 Sixers points and all 121 Bulls points are accounted for in the box score. The quarter scores are StatMuse's and Covers'; the 12-point Sixers lead and Chicago's 7-point lead are Covers' (Yardbarker also has 12; Roundtable has the Bulls up 23–16 in the first). Team totals (rebounds, offensive rebounds, threes, steals, blocks, points in the paint) are Covers'. The Celtics' record and the Sixers' standing are from the site's standings; the 11-game start, the next game and Brown's first regular-season game against Boston are from the AP.

The play of the game is an original illustration of LeBron James's 3-pointer with 8:45 left in the first quarter, assisted by Tyrese Maxey, which cut Chicago's lead from 10–5 to 10–8 (CBS Sports play-by-play). The AP reports it gave him 1,897 career points against Chicago, passing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's 1,895 for the most by any player against the Bulls. The game stories disagree on the order and score of the closing plays (Maxey's late three, Embiid's put-back and free throws, Buzelis's dunk at 1:09), so the late sequence isn't drawn. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as a plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Philadelphia 76ers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to LeBron James's listed 6-foot-9 and 250 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to a reported 7-foot-¼ wingspan (Sportskeeda), in the Sixers' road blue with No. 23 (Wikipedia). It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
